title: LIN-4401 A: Outside-find consequence gate before merge, with docs
description:
## As asked

Piece **A** of LIN-4401 ("What a change spots outside its own area goes into that area's note, not a new ticket"). The parent's `## As asked` block, its full **Implementation Plan** (D1–D7, Places, Witnesses, Budget) and the approving `### Plan Review Verdict` (comment `1a709266-d352-47ce-bba7-d3ea0ddb99d6`) are on LIN-4401. Read them before building.

**Starting point:** LIN-4401's approved plan is where this piece starts. Follow it. Where the code shows it is wrong, change course and say so in a comment on LIN-4401.

## This piece: the pre-merge consequence gate, plus docs (LinearViewer, then one simple-dispatcher PR)

**Approach (D1–D4, D7)**

* Add `CONSEQUENCE_TEST` beside `LEFTOVER_RULE` in the import-free leaf `lib/prompts/leftover-words.js`.
  * A find becomes a ticket only if it **breaks** something, **blocks** work, or **touches safety** (authentication, secrets, data loss, irreversible writes).
  * Where the provider can't create tickets (Jira), the find goes in the summary comment instead.
  * Otherwise it is a `## Waiting` entry in the note of the area its first cited file maps to (`docs/areas/areas.json`, first match wins).
  * Never both.
  * **Unmapped fallback (verdict note 1):** cite a file in the area whose code the find concerns **first**, then the unmapped `tests/` or `scripts/` path. With no file in an area to cite, or no area notes, the find goes in the summary comment, addressed to the person. Do **not** copy the Periodical text's "never to a ticket".
  * Update the header comment so it names both constants and their readers.
* Rewrite `LEFTOVER_RULE`'s outside clause: "a follow-up only close-out files" becomes a Waiting entry in that area's note, with the fallbacks from `CONSEQUENCE_TEST`.
* `lib/dispatch-leftover.js` `leftoverPrompt`:
  * render `CONSEQUENCE_TEST`;
  * the builder writes outside-area leftovers directly into the other area's note on the PR branch;
  * "for close-out" means only a defect the gate sends to a ticket;
  * keep "File nothing yourself."
  * **Verdict note 3:** in the answer wording at `:153` ("tidied / noted / for close-out"), "noted" includes entries written in another area's note.
* `lib/prompt-template-defs.js`, **review**:
  * **Inside or Outside the Ticket's Scope**: review names each outside find's home under `CONSEQUENCE_TEST` (rendered once), either an area slug with the entry worded ready to write, or "ticket" with the consequence that applies and why.
  * **What CI Did Not Prove**: replace the "routed follow-up ticket" and "outside-scope follow-up" clauses.
  * **Hand Off**: "file follow-ups" becomes "file the gate's tickets".
  * The leftover read in **Isolated, or One of a Class?** keeps `LEFTOVER_RULE`.
* `lib/prompt-template-defs.js`, **close-out**:
  * Workflow line 2 covers note entries in any area.
  * Workflow line 5 (`:1024`, "file the outside follow-ups") becomes the gate's tickets.
  * **Make the Fixes Review Asked For** writes every named entry, in its own area or another, before the merge, then re-establishes CI.
  * **Settle the Ledger** Outside bullet (`:1047`): settled by the cited note commit, or by the gate's ticket filed in Triage.
  * **Land It**: the closing sentence's filing clause.
  * **Follow-up Triage** files only gate tickets. Keep the existing-ticket check, priority and label bullets.
  * The `description` field (`:1005`).
* Keep the two axes separate (D4). In-scope work is done or dropped, never filed. "File" appears in ruling options only for an outside item that passes the gate.
* `lib/completion-signals.js` close-out: `coreOutcome`, signals 3 and 6, and `readinessCheck` ("followed-up") speak in the gate's terms.
* `lib/prompts/autopilot-kickoff.js:577` ("files the outside follow-ups").
* Docs:
  * `docs/areas/README.md` ("Who writes here", "One home");
  * `docs/autopilot-operating-manual.md` (ruling-options paragraph, close-out paragraph, and `:496` "the merge, the Done, the summary, the follow-ups");
  * `docs/architecture/dispatch-and-proxy.md` ("What reads the answer");
  * `docs/architecture/prompt-system.md` (LIN-4374 paragraph and the review→close-out paragraph);
  * `public/llms.txt:266` (close-out "…and file follow-ups").
* **Separate one-sentence PR** in JKershaw/simple-dispatcher: `docs/areas/README.md` "One home for each leftover" names `CONSEQUENCE_TEST` beside `LEFTOVER_RULE`.
* Do not add a code guard on ticket creation (D7). Tests hold the shape.
* Out of scope: Periodicals, `retro`, the audit (piece B), and the dated records (`docs/papers/**`, `docs/reviews/**`, `docs/plans/**`, `docs/prompt-pipeline/stage-descriptions/*.md`, eval fixtures and baselines, and the survey census).

**Re-classify the search (verdict note 2).** The plan's "only four unrelated files" claim is wrong: about 110 files hit. Put every live hit in scope or give its out-of-scope reason:
`git grep -n -i -E "follow-up|file it|files it|file the outside|outside item|outside follow" -- lib routes public docs/areas docs/architecture docs/autopilot-operating-manual.md` (both repos)

**Testing**

* New `tests/unit/lin-4401-outside-find-home.test.js`:
  * (i) review, close-out and `leftoverPrompt` each contain `CONSEQUENCE_TEST` exactly once;
  * (ii) it names breaks, blocks and safety with its four kinds;
  * (iii) no rendered stage prompt, kickoff prompt or close-out completion signal carries the retired phrases (build the list from the search, including close-out's `description` and Workflow line 5);
  * (iv) close-out's Follow-up Triage still tells close-out to file a gate ticket.
* Extend `tests/unit/lin-4374-review-leftover-read.test.js`:
  * `RULE_PIECES` gets the new outside clause and `CONSEQUENCE_TEST`'s distinctive pieces (retype guard);
  * the Triage assertion follows the new wording.
* `tests/unit/area-notes.test.js` stays green.
* `tests/unit/prompt-size-budget.test.js`: each ceiling net flat or lower by replacing wording. Any rise needs LIN-4401 and its reason beside the ceiling, in `FROZEN_TOTAL_BYTES` and in the change log, with old reasons moved to Ceiling history. Rebase, then re-measure.
* Add a row to `scripts/prompt-template-change-log.md` (path `template`, expected follow-on direction: down).

**At A's close-out**

* Write the Waiting entry into `docs/areas/llm-and-prompts.md`, citing `lib/prompts/leftover-words.js` first. It says notes now gather where tickets used to, and LIN-4414's one retirement per build drains only touched areas, so rarely touched notes will grow.
* Hand the operator the Done-when check: the first close-out after this merges with an outside find must show a Waiting entry committed before the merge and no ticket that fails the gate. Trend: `scripts/follow-on-ratio.mjs`.

**Acceptance criteria**

* Every live statement of the rule in both repos routes outside finds through `CONSEQUENCE_TEST`. The search re-classification is posted.
* The new and extended tests pass. CI is green. Prompt ceilings are net flat, or any rise is justified as above.
* The LinearViewer PR and the simple-dispatcher PR are both merged. The closing Waiting entry has landed.

Session fit: fits one session

Plan-review due: no — covered by LIN-4401's approving plan-review (comment 1a709266-d352-47ce-bba7-d3ea0ddb99d6, rev 1)

Grounding commits: LinearViewer `94893cc35`, simple-dispatcher `a42456c` (re-checked at breakdown on 12 Nov: both repos are still at these HEADs).

*End of what was asked. Steps write below this line; nothing above it changes.*

comments.body:
## Survey open-0: LIN-4431 @ 94893cc35

*Read at LinearViewer `94893cc35` and simple-dispatcher `a42456c`, the grounding commits. Every anchor the ticket names is where it says.*

**1. "Net flat" can't be reached by swapping words.** At BASE, review renders 16154/16154 bytes, close-out 12182/12182, `leftoverPrompt` 1787/1787, and `FROZEN_TOTAL_BYTES` equals the sum of the ceilings: 0 headroom everywhere. A `CONSEQUENCE_TEST` covering what's asked (three consequences, four kinds of safety, the Jira, unmapped and no-notes fallbacks, "never both") drafts at 490–660 bytes, rendered once in each prompt. The retired wording frees at most about 390 bytes (review), 330 (close-out) and 180 (leftover). Most of that must be replaced, not just deleted, and the ticket adds new asks. Any growth in `LEFTOVER_RULE` counts three times. My forecast: +250–400 bytes each for review and close-out, +20–28% for the leftover prompt. The ceiling-raise paperwork is the likely path, not the exception.

**2. Tests the ticket doesn't list pin the retired wording.** Besides `lin-4374` (`RULE_PIECES`, the Triage assertion):
- `prompt-templates.test.js` has about 11 assertions (:755, :1719, :2379, :2387, :2392, :2512, :2587, :2703, :2713, :2821, :2890). Tests g1, h1 and i5 use "file the outside follow-ups" to mark close-out's step order.
- `lin-4390-periodical-hand-off.test.js:96` and `recommend-stage-assembly.test.js:136` pin the Hand Off sentence being rewritten.
- `tests/judge/audit-report.fixture.json` is a snapshot of close-out's `description` and signals.

**3. Test (iii) would pass without checking two of its targets.** Close-out's `description` and `COMPLETION_SIGNALS` aren't in `generatePrompt` output. The test must read them directly.

**4. The search is mostly noise, with a few real misses.** Of 556 lines, about 425 mean a resumed session, 26 are Periodicals or the audit, about 76 are history comments, and about 29 state the rule. The ticket doesn't list:
- `lib/follow-on-ratio.js:48-49`, which describes close-out as "file follow-ups → merge → Done" (citing a `:946` already stale at BASE). This is the Done-when trend tool.
- `lib/run-ledger.js:165-168` and `render-run-evidence.js:97-101`, which look for "follow-up … LIN-n" in the ledger, so an outside item settled by a note will show no link.

simple-dispatcher needs one sentence; its other lines stay true.

**5. Deeper.** This moves the backlog rather than draining it. Waiting entries have no cap, LIN-4414 retires one entry per build and only in touched areas, and close-out already writes unreviewed note entries (the 10 Nov Security Review entry); now they land in any area's note. The follow-on ratio will fall either way. The notes' Waiting counts (which the guard prints) are the honest measure.

**What I'd do first:** write `CONSEQUENCE_TEST` and the new `LEFTOVER_RULE` clause, then render all three prompts and measure. That number decides whether this is a wording job or a ceiling-raise job, and it's worth saying on LIN-4401 early. Then run `prompt-templates.test.js` against the draft to list every pin that breaks, before touching the docs.

## Survey global: LIN-4431 @ 94893cc35

**Most important: the rule would be stated twice, and the two disagree.** `lib/periodicals.js` already hand-types its own version of the gate: an unmapped finding goes to the person in the closing comment, plus "never to a ticket". This ticket adds `CONSEQUENCE_TEST` and leaves Periodicals out of scope. Both live in `llm-and-prompts` and both write Waiting entries, yet they answer the same case oppositely: a live secret is "never a ticket" for a Periodical and "touches safety, so a ticket" for the gate. Nothing ties them together; the retype guard in `tests/unit/lin-4374-review-leftover-read.test.js` only matches exact strings.

**Where it lands, and the trend.** `lib/prompts/leftover-words.js` is young and improving: LIN-4376 and LIN-4414 pulled shared words into it, guarded against retyping in `lib/` and `routes/`. But only `LEFTOVER_RULE` made it there. The "close-out files outside follow-ups" wording around it is hand-typed in about ten places across `lib/prompt-template-defs.js` (review, close-out), `lib/completion-signals.js` and `lib/prompts/autopilot-kickoff.js`. Done the obvious way, each is rewritten in place as "the gate's tickets", so the gate's wording gets scattered by hand just as the old wording was.

**No room under the size ceilings.** Measured as the size test measures: review 16154/16154, close-out 12182/12182, leftover prompt 1787/1787. Every added byte must be paid for by removing wording, or a ceiling raised with a recorded reason.

**What notices a missed update.**
- CI does, for three tests that pin wording being retired ("or file follow-ups", "file the outside follow-ups"): `tests/unit/prompt-templates.test.js`, `tests/unit/recommend-stage-assembly.test.js`, and `tests/unit/lin-4390-periodical-hand-off.test.js`, a Periodical test. The ticket's test list names none of them.
- Nothing does for `docs/areas/README.md` ("Close-out is the only one that files"), `docs/architecture/*.md`, the operating manual, or simple-dispatcher's README. `public/llms.txt` is only checked for one bullet per template; its close-out line has already drifted.
- Unaffected: `lib/run-ledger.js` and `lib/render-run-evidence.js` read "discharged", not the route; `docs/areas/areas.json` needs nothing, and the area-notes guard already enforces citing a file in the entry's own area first. `lib/follow-on-ratio.js` should fall by design; its comment already cites a stale line.

**Better, at a cost this task can carry:**
- Pay for the gate by cutting restatements, not rewording them. Review's ledger section repeats the inside/outside discharge rule from its scope section; let those spots say "the gate's tickets" and leave the definition to the constant.
- Add the gate's distinctive wording to the retype guard, as planned, and update the three pinning tests deliberately.
- Record the Periodical disagreement as a Waiting entry in the `llm-and-prompts` note, citing `lib/periodicals.js` first.
- Fix the stale citation in `lib/follow-on-ratio.js`.

**Better still, but not this task's:**
- Make Periodicals print `CONSEQUENCE_TEST`. Someone must first rule on the live-secret case.
- A guard over prose copies of the rule in docs, `llms.txt` and the sibling repo.
- The deeper cause: the rule has many hand-typed homes, in prompts with no room to grow. Each new routing rule pays that cost again until the surrounding wording also comes from the shared file.
